tip_title: If You're Not Driving Much, Your Auto Policy Should Reflect That
topic: Auto Insurance - Usage-Based and Low-Mileage Discounts
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: If You're Not Driving Much, Your Auto Policy Should Reflect That**

A lot of people are still paying for auto insurance priced around old driving habits — a long commute, five days a week, multiple road trips per year. If your mileage has dropped (remote work, a shorter commute, a second car that mostly sits in the garage), there's a good chance you're leaving money on the table. Many insurers offer usage-based programs where a mobile app or a plug-in device tracks how much and how safely you drive, then adjusts your premium based on real data rather than assumptions. Drivers who qualify can see meaningful savings — some programs advertise discounts up to 30% for low-mileage or low-risk driving patterns.

Worth a five-minute conversation with your Peachy agent to see if a usage-based program makes sense for how your household actually drives today.

📖 [Learn more from The Zebra](https://www.thezebra.com/auto-insurance/driver/other-factors/car-insurance-low-mileage-drivers/)
summary: Covers usage-based auto insurance programs that track mileage and driving behavior through an app or device, framed as a savings opportunity for households whose driving patterns have changed — lower mileage, remote work, or a secondary vehicle.
scoring_notes: Usage-based auto was covered in July 2026 but that tip was framed as an 'overlooked savings lever worth asking about' in general terms. This tip takes a different angle: specifically targeting households whose driving patterns have shifted (remote work, hybrid schedules, secondary vehicles sitting idle) — a concrete life-stage trigger rather than a generic 'you might save' angle. Strong fit across all three audiences: East Cobb (established families, multiple vehicles, some empty nesters with reduced driving), Perimeter (young professionals, many hybrid/remote workers), and Lewisville Lake (mixed income, family households, college-adjacent younger skew with varying commutes). Actionability is high — readers can ask their agent or download an app this week. Evergreen but not overused. Source (The Zebra) is not on the preferred trusted-source list, but the usage-based discount data is well-established consumer information. No scare tactics, no carrier names, no specific premium promises. Noting the source flag: thezebra.com is a comparison/consumer site with editorial insurance content. The prior tip on this subject (July 20, 2026) was generic; this tip is anchored to a life-change trigger and specific discount mechanism, making it substantively distinct.
